before.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.
Modality applies to this turn's final reply. Progress already streamed earlier in the turn (e.g. Telegram multi_message narration) keeps its streamed modality and is not retracted.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.

after.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.
Modality applies to this turn's final reply. Progress already streamed earlier in the turn (e.g. Telegram multi_message narration) keeps its streamed modality and is not retracted.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.

To deliver output to a configured channel, set delivery={"mode":"announce","channel":"discord","to":"<channel_id_or_chat_id>"}. For webhook deliveries that must thread through the originating conversation, also set delivery.thread_id="<reply_target>". This is the preferred tool for sending scheduled/delayed messages to users via channels.
- cron_list: actions cron_list — List the scheduled cron jobs owned by this agent
- cron_remove: actions cron_remove — Remove a cron job by id or name
- cron_update: actions update — Patch an existing cron job (schedule, command, prompt, enabled, delivery, model, etc.). Accepts job name or ID — no need to call cron_list first.
- cron_run: actions run — Force-run a cron job immediately and record run history
- cron_runs: actions list_runs — List recent run history for a cron job
- schedule: actions schedule_add, cancel, create, get, schedule_list, once, pause, schedule_remove, resume — Manage scheduled shell-only tasks. Actions: create/add/once/list/get/cancel/remove/pause/resume. WARNING: This tool creates shell jobs whose output is only logged, NOT delivered to any channel. To send a scheduled message to Discord/Telegram/Slack/Matrix, use the cron_add tool with job_type='agent' and a delivery config like {"mode":"announce","channel":"discord","to":"<channel_id>"}.

binary_surface.description:
Long-term memory: store a fact, recall it, forget it, export it, or purge it.

Actions:
- memory_store: actions store — Store a fact, preference, or note in long-term memory. Use category 'core' for permanent facts, 'daily' for session notes, 'conversation' for chat context, or a custom category name.
- memory_recall: actions recall — Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or context. Returns scored results ranked by relevance. Supports keyword search, recent recall with omitted query or bare '*', time-only query (since/until), or both.
- memory_forget: actions forget — Remove a memory by key. Use to delete outdated facts or sensitive data. Returns whether the memory was found and removed.
- memory_export: actions export — Export visible memories as a JSON array for GDPR Art. 20 data portability. Supports filtering by namespace, session, category, and time range. Returns a structured, machine-readable JSON array of entries that pass the active memory read policy.
- memory_purge: actions purge — Remove all memories in a namespace or session. Use to bulk-delete per-tenant or per-conversation data. Returns the number of deleted entries. WARNING: This operation cannot be undone.
